people.gloss: Ngọc Hành is the fifth star of the Northern Dipper, the one that weighs
people.role: Head of Thiên Xu Tông and keeper of the Bắc Thần Ấn
people.appearance: A narrow, grey-robed man who looks fifty and always slightly tired, with an accountant's ink-stained middle finger and the stone seal on a cord at his chest.
people.backstory: Doãn Ngọc Hành was born in Thạch Kiều Thành on the night the founder died, under the fifth star of the Dipper, the one that weighs (C147, C148). His family had kept the bridge's toll ledgers since the bridge had tolls, and he could add a column of figures before he could read the names above it. Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) took him at nine, taught him arrays rather than the spear, and in 1150 stepped down for him after 390 years (C187). He was confirmed before the seven seals at Thạch Kiều, and Thính Vũ's seal came a day late (N-thien_xu-08). Four years later he took the Pivot into the Cinnabar Vein War on Phượng Minh's side and beat Thính Vũ at Đan Sơn Mạch (C189, C190); since 1165 his envoys have counted Thính Vũ's disciples every year (C200). He fights from inside his own arrays and governs the same way: slowly, from the centre, by rule. In 1188 he did the one thing the founder forbade. He asked the Chief Judge Phương Trực Ngôn (phuong_truc_ngon) for the Weight, judged Băng Tâm's petition for Tinh Tủy Mạch himself, and refused it (C195, N-thien_xu-09). He gave the Weight back the next morning. He has not explained it to her, to Sở Ngọc Hồ (so_ngoc_ho), or to his own disciples. Two years later, at the Compact-day table, he named Doãn Hi Hòa (doan_hi_hoa) his heir aloud before the elders had been asked, and he has not explained that either.
people.wants: To hand on a Compact that holds without him, and to keep Thính Vũ from the war it is building toward without fighting it.
people.secret: He knows that in 803 the whole guard of Tinh Tủy Mạch was called down to Chiết Kích Nguyên as reinforcements and none came back, so the post stood empty until 806, though no order ever withdrew it (N-thien_xu-04). Under the Compact's own wording an unwatched wild vein might have let Băng Tâm's claim stand. He refused the petition so the Pivot would never lose land by a ruling, and sealed the archive's guard roll for 803 with his own hand. He does not know a second copy was filed among the dead lists of that year, or that it has left the archive. Since a night at the ridge palace in 1154, when Hoa Triêu Dương (hoa_trieu_duong) played him eight airs on what he took for a ridge flute, he cannot hear the seat's single dusk bell without counting eight strokes. He decided for the war the next morning. He lets Bách Vong Ngôn's forbidden zither go, and could not say why. He refuses Ngũ Trấn Bắc's writ each spring because Thính Vũ's spymaster Nhiếp Vô Thanh writes to him through the clerk Tào Mặc Toán, and her numbers are half of Phòng Bách Kế's.

people.role: First elder of Thiên Xu Tông (age 640); its second head, 760-1150, who stepped down for his disciple
people.appearance: Huge and slow, with a miner's shoulders and a seam of grey scar from collarbone to ear; he carries the rebel's spear like a walking staff.
people.backstory: Đỗ Tinh Hà was born in 560 in the black-iron diggings of Huyền Thiết, where a cart carries one ingot (A220), and came up the mountain the same year as two other boys of 560, Quý Trường Kích (quy_truong_kich) and Lôi Vô Danh (loi_vo_danh). Chung Hoài Cực (chung_hoai_cuc) taught all three, and the sect called them the Three of the Same Year. At 200 he became the second head (C147). He called the Pirate Purge (C152), gave Quý the Thiết Mã banner and its tally (C154), and stood on Chiết Kích Nguyên the day Quý fell with ten thousand men and Lôi fled with the banner (C017). He renewed the Compact at the truce (C161), took Hạ Lang Tinh's spear when he destroyed Phá Quân Môn (C163), arbitrated the Long Lake (C171), ended the Thunder Vein War (C179), and killed Mặc Huyết Sinh beside Thôi Khinh Hồng and Sở Ngọc Hồ (C024). In 1150 he stepped down for Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) (C187). He is 640 years old and as patient as a seam of ore. He has looked for Lôi's hiding place for four hundred years and has never said what he would do on finding it.
people.wants: To find the Thiết Mã banner and tally before he dies, and to bury them with Quý under the barrow.
people.secret: He gave the order that sent Quý's army down onto Chiết Kích Nguyên knowing Lạc Hà's miasma array was laid there, because a war ended in one day was cheaper than ten more years of it. Lôi Vô Danh heard him give it, and took the banner so that no one could ever send that army anywhere again.

people.gloss: Square and plain-spoken: trực ngôn is speech that does not bend
people.role: Chief Judge of the Thiên Quyền Hall, who sits at the Bridge Court in Thạch Kiều Thành and holds the Weight
people.appearance: Small, square-shouldered, in the plain grey robe of the bench; she speaks so quietly that the Bridge Court is built to carry her voice.
people.backstory: Phương Trực Ngôn is the daughter of a scale keeper at Thiên Quyền Thị, the market of weight and measure (A207), and she learned to read a beam before she learned to read. The first Chief Judge, Hề Văn Ước (he_van_uoc), heard her at twelve correcting a Pivot assayer in the square and took her to the Bridge Court. She sat behind her master for two centuries, wrote the judgement of the Long Lake for Đỗ Tinh Hà's seal (C171), and took the bench and the Weight of the Heavenly Balance when Hề died in 1062. She formed her Nguyên Anh in 1080 in a cell under Thạch Kiều's bridge. She has heard every claim brought under the Compact since, and she is the only judge whose verdicts Thính Vũ has never appealed. In 1188 she had read Băng Tâm's petition three times and written half her judgement when Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) asked her for the Weight. She gave it, because the head may ask. He judged the claim alone and refused it (C195). She has spoken to him since only on the bench. Her unfinished judgement is in a drawer at the Bridge Court.
people.wants: To finish the 1188 judgement and read it in open court, and to have the rule of the seal and the weight written into the Compact itself, so that no head can take the Weight again.
people.secret: Her unfinished judgement found for Băng Tâm. She does not know why the head took the case, only that she had asked the archive for the vein's guard rolls the day before he did.

people.gloss: Guard of the north; ngũ is a file of five soldiers
people.role: Master of the Dao Quang Hall, the war-writ office: the Pivot's hawk
people.appearance: Square, sunburnt, with cropped grey hair and a soldier's habit of standing at the edge of every room; the iron-hooped drum hangs behind his chair.
people.backstory: Ngũ Trấn Bắc was born in Hoàng Hoa Thôn, a mining village of yellow flowers and Metal soil in Ngọc Hành Sơn, the grandson of a soldier who came home from Chiết Kích Nguyên without his legs (C017). He grew up on the old man's account of that day. Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) took him into the Dao Quang Hall at fifteen and taught him the Army-Breaker Spear, the art the sect took from Phá Quân Môn (C163). He commanded the Pivot's arrays at Đan Sơn Mạch in 1158 and broke Thính Vũ's line there (C190). He formed his Nguyên Anh in 1162, and three years later it was he who sent the envoys to count Thính Vũ's disciples (C200). He has had them counted every year since. The count has doubled twice. He keeps the war-writ office and the drum of the Seventh Star, and he has drafted a writ against Thính Vũ Lâu every spring for thirty-five years. Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) has not sealed one.
people.wants: A war against Thính Vũ Lâu now, while the Pivot can still win it, and the marshal's banner found so that the Pivot has a marshal again.
people.secret: He has traced Lôi Vô Danh's road after 803 from the soldiers' names scratched on the stones of Vi Thành Trại and the old ration rolls, and he is close to the abode on Thiên Tuyền Nguyên. He has told no one, not even Đỗ, because he means to be the one who raises the banner.

people.gloss: One who knows what lies far off
people.role: Master of the Khai Dương Hall and chief envoy of the Pivot
people.appearance: Long-faced and handsome in a dry way, in a robe a shade finer than the seat allows, with the white jade tally hung where a sword would be.
people.backstory: Mâu Tri Viễn was born in Khai Dương Thành, the Pivot's northern road city whose gate faces the morning star (A092), to a clerk of the road tolls and a Tùng Đào boatwoman, and he speaks the river dialects as well as the court's. Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) took him for the Khai Dương Hall in 1018. In the Thunder Vein War he stopped Phượng Minh's raiders at the upper ferry of Thượng Độ with a letter and no escort (A295, C179). Since 1150 he has been master of the hall and chief envoy. He sat at the Pivot's table in 1188 when Ngụy Thanh Hàn (nguy_thanh_han) read Băng Tâm's petition, and he was the one who walked Ngụy to the gate afterward. He keeps the seven guest-houses for the Compact's witnesses at Thạch Kiều, and he knows the habits of every envoy who stays in them. He undoes Ngũ Trấn Bắc's (ngu_tran_bac) writs before they reach the head, by making each one look premature.
people.wants: To make the peace with Thính Vũ Lâu that ends the counting, and to be named first elder for it.
people.secret: In 1197 Công Tôn Duẫn asked him to sound the great sects on whether they would confirm Doãn Hi Hòa, named heir in 1190. He did it, quietly, through their envoys at the witness-houses, and keeps the answers in a sealed letter he has shown no one, not even Công Tôn: four of the seven would refuse her. He is drafting the terms on which Thính Vũ, at least, would change its answer, and the first term is an end to the count.

people.role: Keeper of Tàng Ước Các, the archive of the North Star Compact
people.appearance: Bent and frail, sharp-eyed, black to the wrists from grinding ink; she keeps the archive's keys on a cord around her neck and touches them when she speaks.
people.backstory: Sử Ngưng Mặc was born at the foot of Chấp Bút Phong, the Peak of the Held Brush, where the slate for the sect's inkstones is cut, and was given at seven to Hề Văn Ước (he_van_uoc), who kept the archive as well as the bench in those years. She has kept Tàng Ước Các since 900: the Compact itself, every writ of war since the first in 584 (C118), every arbitration, the land rolls, the guard rolls and the rolls of the 129 boundary steles. She was twenty-eight in 803 and copied the dead lists of Chiết Kích Nguyên by hand for a year (C017). The seat's half of the Thiết Mã tally vanished from her shelves that year; it is the only thing she has ever lost (N-thien_xu-05). She grinds the archive's ink on the founder's inkstone herself and lets no one else touch it. Her disciples Thích Minh Thư (thich_minh_thu) and Hoàng Phủ Tịch (hoang_phu_tich) are the only people she lets past the second door.
people.wants: To find the tally's lost half before her years run out, and to leave the archive to a keeper who will keep it as she has.
people.secret: In 1188 the head came to the archive at night, took the guard roll of Tinh Tủy Mạch for 803, and she sealed the shelf behind him without asking why. She has forgotten that she herself copied a duplicate of it in 803, among the dead lists, without reading what she copied. She has also known since the first ink Họa Tinh Đường sold her archive that its rain-fast stroke is the blood-ink writ of Thorn and Ink Verses with the blood taken out: the copy the Pivot seized at Cửu Thiều Cung's fall (C005) is on her own shelves. She came north to the founder's burial in 1137 to tell Kỷ Ngân Chúc that she would go on buying the ink, and she does.

people.role: The head's chief disciple and steward of the seat; the elders' man
people.appearance: Broad, weathered, in a plain robe with ledger strings at the sleeve; he walks like a man on a deck and keeps a straight blade hanging point-down at his back.
people.backstory: Công Tôn Duẫn is the son of a harbour pilot of Tinh Hán Thành, the Pivot's port built on the old sea-serpent's bones (C067). Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) took him as a disciple in 1024, long before he was head, and Công Tôn formed his core in 1112 holding the Plumb Line his master gave him. For fifty years he has run the seat: its stores, its rosters, its quarrels. He is fair in the seat's daily business, liked by the elders and trusted by the vassals. Everyone assumes he will be the next head except the head, who took a five-year-old girl from Thạch Kiều as his disciple in 1135 (A217) and in 1190 named her heir aloud. Công Tôn trains her in the sword himself, and his own disciple Nhiễm Thừa Nghiệp (nhiem_thua_nghiep) resents her for it. He tells everyone he does not want the Seal.
people.wants: The Seal. He has wanted it for a century and has stopped being ashamed of it.
people.secret: In 1197 he asked the envoy Mâu Tri Viễn to sound the great sects on the named heir, and Mâu has never shown him the answers. The courier Phó Dịch Lam, who carried the replies home, told him which four sects' envoys kept her waiting a month. Now she carries his own letters to those four witness-houses at Thạch Kiều under Mâu's seal, asking whether they would confirm him instead. Each letter says what the seat's night-watch book says, that Doãn Hi Hòa goes into the war-writ office at night, and what she tells him on the training floor, that she agrees with every writ. As steward he keeps that book.

people.role: The head's disciple, named heir aloud in 1190 and not yet confirmed, age 70
people.appearance: Tall and quick, sun-browned, hair tied up with a gold cord; she is always the first on the training floor and the last to leave.
people.backstory: Doãn Hi Hòa was born in Thạch Kiều Thành at sunrise (A217), a descendant, seven generations down, of the head's younger brother, in the house where the Doãn have kept the bridge ledgers since before the Compact. Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) took her as his disciple at five and gave her the founder's method at ten, which no child had been given before. In 1190 he named her his heir aloud at the Compact-day table, before the elders had been asked. She knows what it also says: that a Trúc Cơ of seventy has been put over a Kết Đan of a century's service because she is family. She means to prove it wrong by being better, and has not yet learned that the Pivot does not reward speed. She trains the sword with Công Tôn Duẫn (cong_ton_duan), the man the elders wanted instead of her, and likes him, which makes it worse. In 1158, at twenty-eight, she watched her master break Thính Vũ at Đan Sơn Mạch from a hill (C190), and she has wanted a war of her own since. Her niece Doãn Thường Hi (doan_thuong_hi) has just come up to the outer gate.
people.wants: To be confirmed before the seven seals at Thạch Kiều, and to form her core before she is ninety.
people.secret: Nhiếp Minh Tiễn lets her into the war-writ office at night. She has read every one of Ngũ Trấn Bắc's yearly writs against Thính Vũ, and she agrees with them.

people.role: Copyist of Tàng Ước Các, who found the 803 guard roll and gave it away
people.appearance: Thin and freckled, with soot-grey fingertips and a habit of reading other people's handwriting upside down across a table.
people.backstory: Thích Minh Thư was born in Mặc Yên Thôn, the ink-smoke village whose pine soot fills every inkstick of the sect, and she smelled of it until her twentieth year. Sử Ngưng Mặc (su_ngung_mac) took her into Tàng Ước Các for her hand, the clearest in the archive, and let her recopy the rolls of the boundary steles (N-thien_xu-02). In 1195, recopying the dead lists of Chiết Kích Nguyên (C017), she found a guard roll for Tinh Tủy Mạch filed among them: the vein's whole watch called down to the plain as reinforcements in 803, and the post left empty until 806. She went to the shelf where the archive's own roll should be and found it sealed in the head's hand. She believes the Compact binds the Pivot or binds no one. In 1196 she met Băng Tâm's envoy Ngụy Thanh Hàn (nguy_thanh_han) in a guest-house at Thạch Kiều and gave him a copy (N-thien_xu-10). She has not slept well since, and her rival in the archive, Hoàng Phủ Tịch (hoang_phu_tich), has noticed.
people.wants: To see the Compact kept as it is written, even against the Pivot, and to keep her place in the archive while she does.
people.secret: She is the source of the guard roll Ngụy Thanh Hàn holds. If Băng Tâm brings its second claim, the archive will know the copy by its hand within an hour.

people.role: Founder of Thiên Xu Tông (year 120, at 80) and author of the North Star Compact
people.backstory: Chung Hoài Cực was a hermit's foundling of the Wild Age who reached the Thiên Tuyền plateau at 80 and founded the sect under the Northern Dipper in 120 (C002). He won the ore mountains of Ngọc Hành with fair weights, not swords (C059, A219), and he drank for three days with Kỳ Tùng Ẩn (ky_tung_an) at Thạch Kiều (C070). His first war is still his hardest to defend. In 340 he destroyed Cửu Thiều Cung and its head Lạc Thiều Âm (lac_thieu_am) for music that drew his disciples' minds away (C080, C005), took none of its land, and let the mourners sing over its graves (A236). In 509 he beat Tùng Đào and Lạc Hà together and took no land (C106), and in 510 he set the North Star Compact before the seven sects (C107). In 672 he let Tùng Đào's unlicensed conquest of the Cold Ford stand for an old friend's sake (C136), which the Pivot counts as his one bad judgement. He died at 720 on the night Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) was born (C147, C148). He lies under Thái Nhất Phong, facing the pole.

people.role: Thiên Xu Tông's war marshal in the War of Broken Halberds; held the ramparts of Cố Lũy
people.backstory: Quý Trường Kích was a goatherd's son from Thạch Dương Thôn who came up the mountain in the cohort born in 560, with Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) and Lôi Vô Danh (loi_vo_danh), the Three of the Same Year. At forty he carried the halberd Trầm Sa Kích that Thối Tinh Môn forged him from star iron (C124). He sailed in the Pirate Purge (C152), and in 785 Đỗ made him war marshal and gave him the Thiết Mã banner and its tally (C154). Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ broke the Compact in 790 (C016), and in 798 he raised the ramparts of Cố Lũy at the plain's edge and held them five years (A212), with his son Quý Bất Hối (quy_bat_hoi) beside him and his son's wife pregnant in the signal post behind. In 803 he took the army down onto Chiết Kích Nguyên on Đỗ's order, and the war ended that day (C017). He lies under the Vạn Cốt Trủng with his halberd, whose iron has not worn away (C160). The plain is still poisoned.

people.backstory: The third of the Three of the Same Year and Quý Trường Kích's (quy_truong_kich) lieutenant. He came off Chiết Kích Nguyên alive in 803 with the Thiết Mã banner and was never seen in the sect again (C017). He hid for 147 years in a cave abode on Thiên Tuyền Nguyên, inside the Pivot's own plain, and died there in 950. The sect calls him a deserter and a thief. No one has asked why he took the banner and not the tally.

people.backstory: A Thạch Kiều scribe's daughter whom Chung Hoài Cực (chung_hoai_cuc) made the first Chief Judge in 510 and gave the Weight of the Heavenly Balance, with the rule that the one who seals does not weigh (N-thien_xu-01). She wrote the Compact's wording (C107), ground its ink, and kept the archive and the bench together for four centuries. She taught Phương Trực Ngôn (phuong_truc_ngon) and Sử Ngưng Mặc (su_ngung_mac). She died on the bench in 1062, between two cases.
